newsitem.title: CHINA: China's demand for healthy food outstrips supply.
newsitem.headline: China's demand for healthy food outstrips supply.

text.p: Demand for organic food in China is outstripping supply, despite a 71.4 percent rise in production last year that brought annual output to 3.6 million tonnes, the China Business Daily said on Sunday.
China would increase the percentage of cultivated land used to grow food without chemicals to 1.0 percent by 2000, from 0.1 percent in 1990, the newspaper said.
Agricultural authorities planned to create new organic food "production bases" in 10 major cities by the end of the century, it quoted Li Lintao of the China Green Food Development Centre as saying.
"Our aim is to lead more farmers to produce green food," Li said.
The organic food industry's estimated annual output value was 15 billion yuan ($1.8 billion), the newspaper said.
Beijing would promote the use of environmentally-friendly pesticides and would ban the use of fodder additives after 2000, it said, but gave no details.
